03-001.r: A simple machine (pulley, lever, wheel, screw) lets a person do the same amount of work with less force.

03-002.r: A man inhaling deeply on a sensitive balance → reading increases: inhaled air adds mass (1 litre air ≈ 1.225 g; a 4.8 litre breath ≈ 5.88 g).

03-003.r: Vector = magnitude + direction (displacement, velocity, force); scalar = magnitude only (volume).

03-005.r: Speed is a scalar; velocity, torque and displacement are vectors.

03-006.r: Pressure (force per unit area, acting in all directions) is a scalar; force, velocity and acceleration are vectors.

03-007.r: Vectors: velocity, displacement, acceleration, momentum, force. Scalars: distance, volume, speed, pressure, energy, work, density.

03-008.r: Momentum = mass × velocity, so momentum ÷ velocity = mass.

03-009.r: Force = mass × acceleration (F = m·a); a force changes an object's velocity, i.e. accelerates it.

03-010.r: Non-contact forces act without physical contact: magnetic, gravitational and electric forces. Friction and impact forces need contact.

03-011.r: Cube with volume equal to surface area: l³ = 6l² → edge l = 6 units.

03-012.r: Law of conservation of energy → energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it only changes form or is transferred.

03-013.r: Not from the Sun's energy: nuclear energy (from the atomic nucleus) and geothermal energy (Earth's internal heat, radioactive decay). Biomass and wind are solar-derived.

03-014.r: Wind energy is only kinetic energy (air in motion); it can be converted into mechanical and electrical energy.

03-015.r: Wind power: turbines turn the wind's kinetic energy into mechanical power, which a generator converts into electricity.

03-016.r: Friction during motion turns kinetic energy into heat; static friction does no work (no displacement, no energy change).

03-017.r: Light → electric: solar cell; electric → sound: loudspeaker; mass → heat: nuclear reactor; chemical → heat and light: fuel combustion.

03-018.r: Galileo Galilei first defined speed: distance covered per unit time (v = d/t); Newton later gave the laws of motion.

03-019.r: Newton's first law = Law of Inertia: a body stays at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless an unbalanced force acts.

03-020.r: Train starts suddenly → passenger's head leans backward: inertia of rest (lower body moves with the train, upper body stays at rest).

03-021.r: Bus turns sharply right → passengers lean to the left: the lower body turns with the bus, the upper body keeps moving in the old direction.

03-022.r: Statics → branch of mechanics dealing with bodies at rest.

03-023.r: A (man on frictionless surface moves by whistling: Newton's third law) and R (no external force → momentum unchanged) are both true; R doesn't explain A.

03-024.r: Walking on ice is hard because ice offers less friction than the rough road surface.

03-025.r: Box pushed at constant velocity → zero acceleration → zero net force, so friction equals the applied force: 200 N.

03-026.r: Static friction is greater than kinetic friction, so starting a loaded cart needs a harder push than keeping it moving.

03-027.r: Goalkeeper pulls hands back → longer time to stop the ball → smaller rate of change of momentum → less force on hands (F = m(v − u)/t).

03-028.r: 'Every action has an equal and opposite reaction' → Newton's third law of motion (forces act in pairs).

03-029.r: Centripetal ('centre-seeking') force keeps a body moving along a circular path; without it the body would move in a straight line.

03-030.r: Coriolis force → an inertial (fictitious) force on moving objects in a rotating frame; on Earth it results from Earth's rotation.

03-031.r: Momentum conservation: man × 5 m/s = boat × 0.5 m/s → the boat's mass is 10 times the man's.

03-032.r: de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p = h/mv; ball of 0.12 kg at 20 m/s → λ = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ ÷ (0.12 × 20) = 2.76 × 10⁻³⁴ m.

03-033.r: Equal kinetic energies and equal stopping forces → truck, car and motorcycle stop in the same distance (X = Y = Z).

03-034.r: KE = ½mv²; same mass → KE ratio 4 : 9 gives velocity ratio √4 : √9 = 2 : 3.

03-035.r: Ball bearings reduce the effective area of contact between wheel and axle → less friction.

03-036.r: Ball bearings convert static friction into rolling friction; they reduce rotational friction and support radial and axial loads.

03-037.r: Car on a straight level road (or at rest) is in vertical equilibrium: weight shared equally, so reaction at each wheel stays R.

03-038.r: Partly filled oil tanker accelerating forward → oil surface tilts, with greater depth at the rear end.

03-039.r: Vehicle on a sharp circular path at high speed → skids outwards and overturns about its outer wheels (statements 1 and 3).

03-040.r: A rolling ball stops because friction, an external force, opposes its motion; without friction it would keep rolling.

03-041.r: Equal halves of a distance at speeds v₁ and v₂ → average speed = 2v₁v₂ / (v₁ + v₂), not (v₁ + v₂)/2.

03-042.r: Acceleration a = (v − u)/t, from v = u + at (v final velocity, u initial velocity, t time).

03-043.r: From rest: s = ½at² → 400 = ½ × a × 20² → a = 2 m/s²; F = ma = 7000 kg × 2 = 14000 N.

03-044.r: Work W = F × s × cos θ; force along the motion → W = 140 N × 15 m = 2100 joule.

03-045.r: Washing machine works on centrifugation: centrifugal force separates particles by size, shape and density.

03-046.r: Cream separates from milk on churning due to centrifugal force.
03-046.h: Spin to separate: washing machine dryer and cream churning both use centrifugal force.

04-001.r: Brahmagupta (7th century AD, born Bhinmal, Rajasthan) declared in 'Brahmasphuta Siddhanta' that all things gravitate to the Earth, anticipating Newton.

04-002.r: Isaac Newton → universal law of gravitation (1687, 'Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy'): force ∝ product of masses, ∝ 1/distance².

04-004.r: Astronauts can't stand erect in space: no gravity (microgravity) makes them weightless; muscles and bones also weaken.

04-005.r: An apple released from an orbiting spaceship moves along with the spaceship at the same speed.

04-006.r: Leaning Tower of Pisa stands because the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls within its base.

04-007.r: Gravity follows the inverse square law (F = GMm/r²): doubling the Earth–Sun distance makes the force one-fourth.

04-008.r: A falling object's weight stays the same (ideal case, no air resistance): its mass and gravity do not change.

04-009.r: In vacuum, a feather, rubber ball and wooden ball dropped together land together: no air resistance, same acceleration for all.

04-010.r: Equal-size pieces of wood, wax and iron dropped from the same height (air resistance negligible) land at the same time: same g for all.

04-011.r: Iron and wooden balls of the same weight dropped in air: the smaller iron ball lands first, the larger wooden one later (air resistance); in vacuum, together.

04-012.r: Balls of 10 kg and 1 kg dropped from 20 m land together: final velocity V = √(2gh) does not depend on mass.

04-013.r: Objects of different masses falling freely near the Moon's surface (dropped together) have the same velocity at any instant.

04-014.r: Falling body: potential energy turns into kinetic energy, so conservation of energy is not violated; gravity (a conservative force) is not violated either.

04-015.r: Moon's surface gravity is 1/6 of Earth's, so a person weighs 1/6 there: A true; R ('Moon has no gravity like Earth') false.

04-016.r: Weight is maximum at the poles: Earth is flattened at the poles, so the polar radius is less than the equatorial radius and g is greater.

04-018.r: If Earth spins faster, centrifugal force (maximum at the equator, acting against gravity) grows → a body's weight at the equator decreases.

04-019.r: Free fall from rest: d = ½gt² → the displacement–time graph is a parabola.

04-020.r: A body sliding from rest down a smooth incline of angle θ moves with acceleration g sin θ instead of g.

04-021.r: Ball dropped from rest: v = u + at = 0 + 9.8 × 3 = 29.4 m/s after 3 seconds.

04-022.r: Gravity g = GM/R²: if radius shrinks by 1% (0.99 R) with the same mass, g' = 1.02 g, i.e. g increases by 2%.
04-022.h: Since g ∝ 1/R²: radius down 1% → g up about 2%.

04-023.r: Destructive earthquake → ground acceleration greater than 980 cm/s² (9.8 m/s²).

04-024.r: Mass does not change with gravity: 100 kg on Earth is 100 kg on the Moon; only weight changes (Moon's g = g/6).
04-024.t: Don't confuse mass (constant) with weight (changes with gravity).

04-025.r: Weightlessness → no supporting force on the body, as in free fall; this condition is called 'zero gravity'.

04-026.r: We don't feel Earth's orbital motion because we move with the Earth: our speed relative to Earth along its orbit is zero.
04-026.c: The question's figure 'about 4,400 km per hour' is far below Earth's real orbital speed; remember only the reason, not this number.

04-027.r: If Earth's gravity vanished, an object's weight would become zero but its mass would stay the same.

04-028.r: A satellite does not fall because Earth's gravitational pull provides the centripetal acceleration for its curved orbit.

04-029.r: A satellite stays in orbit by centripetal force, supplied by Earth's gravity; gravity likewise keeps planets moving around the Sun.

04-031.r: Four fundamental forces: gravity is the weakest, strong nuclear the strongest (holds protons and neutrons); weak nuclear causes radioactivity; electromagnetism acts on charges.

04-032.r: Lift accelerating upward → apparent weight w = m(g + a) → the person feels heavier.

04-033.r: A pendulum's time period depends on its effective length, not its mass; longer length → longer period.

04-034.r: Pendulum clocks lose time in summer: heat lengthens the pendulum → longer time period → clock runs slow.

04-035.r: Girl stands up on a swing → centre of gravity rises → effective length shortens → period becomes shorter.

04-036.r: Pendulum: acceleration zero at mean position; a given velocity is reached twice per cycle; amplitude falls with time. Statement 3 wrong: acceleration is maximum at extremes.

04-037.r: Pendulum clock runs fast in winter: cold contracts the pendulum, shortening its period.
04-037.h: Summer slow, winter fast: heat lengthens, cold shortens the pendulum.

04-038.r: Earth's escape velocity = 11.2 km/s: the minimum speed needed to escape a celestial body's gravitational field.

04-039.r: Object thrown at 8 km/s returns to Earth: it is below the escape velocity of 11.2 km/s.

04-040.r: Moon has no atmosphere: low g → low escape velocity, which is less than the RMS velocity of gas molecules, so gases escaped.

04-042.r: A (candle in space gives no flame) and R (a flame exists due to gravity) both true, R explains A (NASA experiment).

04-043.r: In weightlessness (microgravity) a candle flame becomes spherical.
